findings.title: The Detail tab's complete/fail taps CANNOT succeed from an agentless panel (now proven, previously unproven)
findings.why: the panel calls executeTool({name, arguments}) without `agent`; the adapter forwards `agent` only when supplied; the tool's sessionIdOf(exec) then answers the agentless sentinel "workspace", so caller = ["workspace"], isOwner is false for every owned row and recordNamesLead is false → casCloseTask refuses with the owner/lead sentence, which the tap shows verbatim. A completed tap is therefore impossible, not merely unproven.
findings.direction: decide the identity question for native taps: either hide/disable complete/fail when the panel carries no agent, or give the team tools a documented HUMAN channel (the app tap is the user, not a member), or have the panel resolve the owning member. Do NOT widen owner-only.

findings.title: §7.2 rule 6's task clause is not implemented (badge for kind/status, timeline for a task's life)
findings.why: Board rows carry status as list `trailing` text and a subtitle; the Detail tab renders keyValue rows and no badge, and neither panel contains a timeline. Members DO match the rule (initials badge + name + mode). A `list` row cannot contain a badge node, so the rule as written is partly inexpressible — it needs a stated row form.
findings.direction: restate rule 6 for list rows (`trailing` + `tone`, or a Detail badge) and either add the Detail timeline or amend the rule; do not leave a BINDING rule unmet.

findings.title: The Memory tab ignores `memory.dir` and never reads the global store
findings.why: the documented layout is `<workspace>/<memory.dir or ".mpd">/memory/agents/<slug>/…`; the panel hard-codes `.mpd`, so a workspace that configures `memory.dir` shows the empty state while entries exist. The global store (`<HOME>/.mpd/memory`, `memory.globalDir`, written by mpd_memory_write scope:"global") is never read, so a workspace with only global entries also reads as empty. The frontmatter format (JSON), the entry directory and the reflection.json keys do match the documented store.
findings.direction: resolve the effective memory dir (the same config the row reads) and either declare the tab workspace-only in its copy or read the global store too; a service would remove the whole class.

findings.title: hold/resume can succeed, but the tool resolves a DIFFERENT workspace root than the panel
findings.why: the panel resolves the team id from its own scoped workspace, but the tool's exec has no agent, so workspaceRoot falls back to DSH_WORKSPACE_ROOT → process.cwd(). In a composition where those differ from the session's workspace the hold is written to (or looked up in) the wrong store while the toast says it landed. No identity gate exists, which is why this one CAN succeed — the risk is the root, not the caller.
findings.direction: do not route a mutation through a tool when the caller has no session; either add hold/resume to the mpdWatchdog service (already the read seam) or have the adapter pass a workspace-bound exec.

findings.title: The Memory tab merges every agent slug, orders by mtime and shows 10, while mpd_memory_read is per-agent and filename-ordered
findings.why: with per-agent `memory.agentSlug` overrides the tab shows another agent's entries; neither ordering matches the tool, so the tab and `mpd_memory_read` can disagree about 'the latest'
findings.direction: state the scope in the tab copy, or filter by the session's agent slug

findings.title: Legacy reflection.json keys are not tolerated
findings.why: the memory row itself accepts `reflected_completed_steps` / `steps_since_last_successful_reflection`; the panel's reader does not, so an old state file shows 0/0
